verdict.rationale: WorkOS AuthKit Connect documents OAuth applications for third parties. These are apps built by customers or partners that show a "Sign in with [your application]" button and use the authorization_code flow against AuthKit, which the docs call a spec-compatible OAuth authorization server. That directly delivers the story of turning your app into an OAuth provider. Missing for 10: documentation of token issuance details (scopes, consent screen, refresh/ID token specifics) and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can turn my own application into an OAuth provider that issues tokens to third-party clients ("Sign in with my app")

citations.quote: A third-party OAuth application will generally have a "Sign in with [your application]" button on their login page
Select third-party when the application is one built by your customers or partners, but you do not directly control the integrating application.
OAuth applications use the underlying `authorization_code` OAuth flow
AuthKit, which is a spec-compatible OAuth authorization server.
